options.name: Developer columns
options.description: Existing candidate: visible developer columns and a shared backlog

options.name: Expandable queues
options.description: Existing candidate: compact owner rows with expandable queues

options.name: Dispatch ledger
options.description: An editorial operations ledger: wide horizontal ticket rows with a narrow owner rail, stamped priority numerals, ink/navy on white. Assignment happens inline in each row; not cards in developer columns.

options.name: Horizontal swimlanes
options.description: One horizontal lane per developer, tickets sequenced left-to-right. Unassigned is a docking strip above. Bright blue/white transit-planning utility. Make the timeline-like reading order feel unmistakable; no invented dates.

options.name: Ownership orbit
options.description: A radial planning diagram: developer stations around a central unassigned hub. Ticket selection lights a destination station; clicking station assigns. Crisp SVG geometry and a small priority inspector, plum and pale lavender. Keep actual tickets readable, not decorative bubbles.

options.name: Command desk
options.description: Keyboard/search-first assignment console, large command input with concrete ticket suggestions, developer destination actions and one focused queue preview. Clean light command launcher with dark command region. Support selecting a real ticket then owner and priority; do not fake command execution.

options.name: Allocation sheet
options.description: Spreadsheet allocation: all eight ticket rows, columns for title, kind, points, editable owner, priority; tight data grid, row selection, spreadsheet-style blue active cell. Inline selects and move up/down actions, not boards.

options.name: Ticket inspector
options.description: Master-detail workbench: compact ticket list left, substantial editable inspector right, developer roster as navigation. Calm gray/teal desktop tool. Selecting ticket reveals assignment and priority editor; all actual fields visible.

options.name: One ticket at a time
options.description: Focused triage deck: one large current ticket, progress through eight tickets, three clearly differentiated owner destinations plus backlog, small queue summaries. Warm orange/white with oversized content and minimal chrome. Assignment advances deck, previous/next allow revisiting, order editable.

options.name: Magnetic planning board
options.description: Freeform spatial planning mat with four labeled owner territories and ticket tiles, not a four-column kanban. Asymmetric 2D zones, subtle paper material, restrained colored tape-like headers. Real native drag/drop between territories plus click assignment controls and priority shifts.

options.name: Team routes
options.description: Metro diagram metaphor implemented as real SVG lines/stops for Maya, Leo, Priya and backlog. Tickets are labeled stops in priority order; selecting stop opens compact move control. White background, three colored route lines, typography carrying actual content; no invented analytics.

options.name: Point shelves
options.description: Inventory shelf allocation: developer shelves made of ticket blocks sized by actual points, with readable list below/alongside; unassigned bins. Ochre/charcoal workshop palette. Points are informational, never enforce imaginary capacity. Selecting block assigns and shifts priority.

options.name: Sprint inbox
options.description: Email-client-style triage: folder rail for owners, compact subject list with selection, reading pane and assign toolbar. Blue-gray professional mail aesthetic; backlog is inbox, ticket details and ownership are real. Support multi-select assignment if simple; individual assignment/reordering essential.

options.name: Priority ladders
options.description: Three vertical numbered priority ladders, but tickets live on horizontal rungs spanning a shared ranking grid with backlog parked in a separate drawer. Strong numeric hierarchy and square lavender/black controls. Emphasize priority slots and move-to-rung rather than generic owner cards.

options.name: Planning strips
options.description: Calendar-like planner without fabricated dates: numbered priority slots across top, people down side, tickets occupying cells with real points labels. Spacious mint-white grid, backlog strip, selecting cell/ticket and assigning to an owner/slot. Label columns Priority 1,2,3 rather than time.

options.name: Transfer desk
options.description: Dual-pane file-manager transfer UI: choose source owner left and destination owner right; pick tickets and transfer with center controls; up/down priority in either list. Dense dark slate utility, high clarity, breadcrumb-like owner controls. Distinct from comparing UI candidates—this is ownership transfer within one candidate.

options.name: Team outline
options.description: Outliner: owner headings and indented numbered ticket lines in one flowing document, folding optional. Typewriter-like white workspace, coral selection bar, compact inline assignment controls. Real moving between headings and reorder lines, not four expanded card queues.

options.name: Assignment mosaic
options.description: Dense chips grouped into an asymmetric owner mosaic. Small ticket IDs expand selected chip into a full-width detail band; ownership selection via compact segmented control. Saturated cobalt regions with legible white and yellow highlights. Keep full titles accessible through selection and show actual counts.

options.name: Terminal planner
options.description: A genuinely terminal-shaped task planner with fixed-width rows, numbered commands, command history/status and highlighted selected row. Amber on dark brown, no fake system telemetry. Real click/keyboard commands for owner assignment and priority; explain accepted commands and retain ordinary accessible buttons.

options.name: Blueprint workbench
options.description: Drafting-table layout: ticket specifications on left, ownership placement diagram on right with technical dimension/priority labels derived only from actual data. Blueprint navy/cyan drawing surface; crisp linework and real controls. Grid justified as actual placement canvas, not decorative background.

options.name: People first
options.description: People-centric roster: large typographic developer profiles arranged asymmetrically, each with assigned work as a readable numbered editorial list. A shared ticket tray and selected-person assign panel. Warm red/white humanist look, initials not stock avatars. Selecting person is the primary navigation.

options.name: Assignment matrix
options.description: Ticket-by-developer assignment matrix: eight rows and four owner columns, a single selected ownership cell per row, with points and priority displayed. High-contrast black/white and emerald selected cells. Clicking a cell reassigns; separate tiny priority arrows reorder. This should read as a decision matrix at a glance.
